title: Motorik
brief: Build a self-running, clock-locked bassline -- no keyboard this time, it plays itself. This is the mid-1970s Kraftwerk/Giorgio Moroder idea (Autobahn, 1974; Donna Summer's "I Feel Love", 1977): the sequencer isn't an accessory to a band, it *is* the band, ticking out a mechanically exact pattern no drummer or bassist would ever play so precisely. Four modules, no more: Clock -> Sequencer, then the Sequencer's "CV" jack into the VCO's "1V/Oct" jack (each step becomes a different pitch), and the VCO through the VCF into the Output. Set a handful of the Sequencer's step sliders to different heights so it actually plays a pattern rather than one repeated note -- a flat, unvarying row of steps is silent on the one thing this level checks. For an extra edge, patch the Sequencer's own "Gate" jack into the VCF's "CV" jack too: the same per-step pulse that just played a note also snaps the filter brighter on every step, without needing an envelope generator at all.
